decisions.covered: Independence I in Peary Land, Saqqaq at Qeqertasussuk and Nipisat, existing Early Dorset at Sermermiut, Inuit life at Qilakitsoq
heldQuestions: Do not substitute the museum's broad cultural dates for exact occupation dates of individual Independence I houses.
Late Dorset and early Thule still need additional site-specific date series; the detailed Natmus account places Thule's arrival in Greenland around 1200, not an unqualified 1000.
Aasivissuit seasonal inland hunting is securely documented, but no new dated point is supplied here until its individual phases are recovered from the nomination/site report.

decisions.covered: Norse settlements and material connections are in norse.json; here Tuperna's family farming, Nuuk mission/provisioning buildings, Thule commerce and an East Greenland town anchor later history.
heldQuestions: Earlier Inuit use of all these regions remains distinct from colonial town-foundation dates.
Dundas/old Thule must not be plotted at modern Qaanaaq.
The 1934 limit is a display cap, not evidence of abandonment; no cessation is fabricated.

decisions.covered: Early settlement archaeology, assembly and episcopal places, Hanseatic harbour commerce, workshop-town development, 1918 sovereignty and 1934 franchise.
heldQuestions: The papar account is now represented at Ari’s supported composition window, 1122–1133. Earlier Irish presence remains uncertain; no pre-Norse settlement interval or voyage route is inferred.
The 871 ± 2 tephra association is not an exact first-arrival date.
Later Icelandic demographic, fisheries and regional port history remains partial; these dated points are a bounded coverage expansion rather than a claim of exhaustive national history.

decisions.region: Norse retreat, Icelandic continuity and the papar tradition
decisions.covered: Four new records, a corrected Eastern Settlement regional end, and a contextual story from settlement to 1934.
heldQuestions: Individual Greenland farms require their own dated occupation sequences; the regional endpoints do not assign identical lifetimes to every building.
Papar are later textual testimony; no exact arrival date, monastery site, Dicuil itinerary or Brendan route is verified.
Greenland’s selected later dated communities are not replaced with an unsupported all-island continuous population interval.

norseHeldQuestions.reason: No two independently day-dated anchors were recovered for Leif, Bjarni, Karlsefni or Gudrid. Coarse evidence records and activities express the supportable connections without invented January dates.
1021 is a cutting/activity date. It does not identify a landfall day, first arrival year or named crew.
L'Anse aux Meadows is on Newfoundland, across the Strait of Belle Isle from Labrador. The province name contains both.

norseHeldQuestions.decision: Keep proposed identifications out of confirmed-site layers
norseHeldQuestions.reason: Wallace's Gulf of St Lawrence and northeastern New Brunswick reconstruction is an interpretation, not an excavated Norse Hóp site.

norseHeldQuestions.decision: No transaction arrow at L'Anse aux Meadows
norseHeldQuestions.reason: Sagas describe encounters, but the local archaeological evidence does not identify a particular transaction or community. Norse objects in Arctic Indigenous contexts can involve multiple mechanisms.
Imported taxa are identified, but the particular American forest or embarkation place is unresolved; no source-to-farm line with invented endpoint is added.

Western Settlement c.1350 and Eastern Settlement mid-fifteenth-century ends are explicitly inferred regional anchors. The 1408 wedding is a separate dated attestation, not an abandonment date. No precise last-person departure or destination is asserted.

norseNotes: The stable lanse-1021 record is retained unchanged; the guide and additional records link to it rather than duplicating the annual cutting claim.
New schematic connections are EvidenceRecord movements, not VoyageTrack objects. Activities deliberately have no relatedVoyageIds because no exact dated track represents the same party.
The compiled north-atlantic-history.json supplies 17 further place-based records across Greenland and Iceland; it is complementary to this package.
No media assets were downloaded or edited. Map source discovery, figure identifiers, license evidence and intended use are supplied for the integrating agent.

norseContinuityDecisions.decision: Revise existing deep-no-qassiarsuk-farms rather than create a duplicate Eastern regional occupation marker. The title, interpretation and end note explicitly identify the regional scope.
endEvidence.start=endEvidence.end at 1350 or 1450 is a display anchor with inferred certainty and an approximate label. No invented plus/minus confidence interval or exact final-departure claim.
Use c.1000 for the Western regional record to express late-tenth/early-eleventh-century occupation. Keep c.985 for the Eastern region. These do not assign the same foundation year to every farm.
Keep deep-no-igaliku-imported-wood as an attestation of material evidence. Its 1100–1400 dates are not a whole settlement occupation interval.
Add an island-wide 870–1934 habitation with history.continuity=ongoing and endMeaning=unknown. Use the existing Icelanders identity, not eternal Viking culture; 1934 is the coverage cutoff.
Add the source-verified wedding on 1408-09-16. Omit a construction-to-abandonment church interval because the present source pass does not establish that full chronology.

Add the textual account at its supported composition window 1122–1133, with a separate under-discussion presence claim. Regional coordinate refers to the text’s subject. Do not assign pre-Norse monks a population interval or route.
Discuss Dicuil only as a debated comparison in the cited scholarship; do not manufacture a c.795 journey from an uncertain identification of Thule. No Brendan legend is represented as a real track.

Ari publisher PDF downloaded via HTTP after HTTPS timeout; p.xiii composition, p.4 chapter 1 and p.17 note18 read. Chapter 1 and NKA report p.14 rendered and visually checked. PNAS full XML retrieved from EuropePMC. Private research files retained.

Integrated reviewed records, guide sections and a contextual story; added Iceland and Western Settlement markers to the existing North Atlantic extent. No new map extent or terrain asset was created. Existing local Greenland evidence anchors later scenes.
